ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=30^\circ$, $AC=2\sqrt{3}$, $\tan B=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, find the length of $AB$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the diagram, draw $CD \perp AB$ at point D,\\
$\therefore \angle ADC=\angle BDC=90^\circ$\\
$\because \angle A=30^\circ$, $AC=2\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore CD=\frac{1}{2}AC=\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore AD=\sqrt{AC^{2}-CD^{2}}=3$\\
$\because \tan B=\frac{CD}{BD}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$,\\
$\therefore BD=2$,\\
$\therefore AB=AD+BD=\boxed{5}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a triangle ABC, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is above, and the base AB is approximately horizontal. According to the problem statement, ∠A = 30°, AC = 2√3, and tan B = √3/2 is given. Then reason: According to the method, let A = (0,0), and let AB be in the positive direction of the x-axis, so B = (x,0). Because AC = 2√3 and ∠A = 30°, the coordinates of point C are (2√3 cos30°, 2√3 sin30°) = (3, √3). From the position of the figure, C is above AB, and the foot of the perpendicular is between A and B, so B is to the right of C, the horizontal distance is x - 3, and the vertical distance is √3. Thus tan B = opposite side/adjacent side = √3/(x - 3) = √3/2, solving gives x - 3 = 2, so x = 5, therefore AB = 5.
